The search result identifies the correct Moon page. I’m fetching that page directly to locate its minimum perigee value.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=20000)
print(moon_page)
```
I’m fetching Kipchoge’s page separately to confirm the record-making marathon time used for his pace.
```python
kipchoge_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge", max_chars=16000)
print(kipchoge_page)
```
I have the requested distance basis from the Moon reference and am now calculating the hours using 2:01:09 over 42.195 km, then rounding to the nearest 1000 hours.
```python
time_hours = 356400 / (42.195 / (2 + 1/60 + 9/3600))
rounded_hours = round(time_hours / 1000) * 1000
print(rounded_hours)
```
17000 hours
